I see

en: As for taking over the family,
why are you hesitating?
it were someone else's business, but do you
note: Continues M1#1902 (slice 023): that row must end 'You speak of your own family as if'.

en: dislike your family's power?
I see
Who's there?!
It's me.
note: Standalone line (msg 75574): 'It's me.' - could be the start of a longer cut-off phrase; kept short.

en: What seems to be the trouble?
An extremely noble
note: Rows 1930-1944 (no used_in except 1941-1944): Christopher's entranced mumbling (1930-1934, 1938) and a speaker with honorific speech (1935-1937, 1939-1940), inferred as Mrs. Stanberg from msg 279847 (scream 'Gya'+'a'x4). Trailing spaces inside fragments assume plain concatenation.

en: bloodline, the
note: Joined: 'An extremely noble bloodline, the Stanberg family'.

en: Stan
berg family
What on earth is the matter with you?
You turn up in the dead of night, mumbling
and muttering things that make no sense.
Noble...
note: Single word, read as the player muttering again; ellipsis added to mark mumbling.

en: Are you even conscious?
Come on, pull yourself together.
Gya
note: Pairs with #1942 'a' (x4) in msg 279847, where M1#6833 (slice 085) must be 'Gya' so it reads 'Gyaaaaa!'. This row itself is not used by a known message.

en: a
note: Lengthening mark: one 'a' each, printed four times after M1#6833 'Gya'.

en: Delicious.
It's too delicious.
note: No speaker tag (msg 75775): continues the player's line from #1943.

en: Pleased to meet you, sir.
I do business down at the market,
note: Joined with #1947: 'I do business down at the market, and the name's Emil.'

en: and the name's Emil.
Oh, the market, is it?
My shop's just north of Market Street.
Sir, do drop by and see me.
Sir, come and visit the market too,
please.
note: Shared by msgs 78505/78599/79283/79421; lead rows (#1951, #2040, #2044) must end with a verb phrase like 'visit the market too,'.

en: , sir!
note: After NAME: 'NAME, sir!'; fits #803 'Ah, it's ' + NAME + ', sir!'.

en: Well now, you're up awfully early today!
, sir! Look who it is!
note: After NAME: 'NAME, sir! Look who it is!' (Japanese: 'if it isn't NAME-danna!').

en: Thanks for being such a loyal customer,
it really helps me out.
Don't suppose a sweet deal's lying around
somewhere, eh...
Business is booming, thanks to you!
I can't stop grinning. Ha ha ha!
Welcome to this humble shack, sir.
Next time, visit the market too,
note: Msg 79564 continues with M1#2050, which then needs 'please,' (and presumably 'young master!' after it).

en: please, sir!
Hey there, welcome!
Sir, let me say that more often at the market,
if you don't mind.
Rather than lounge about at home, I'm more
at ease when I'm working, I tell ya...
So, sir, by all means come to the market,
please!
note: Completes #1970: 'by all means come to the market, / please!'

en: Welcome!
And it's all thanks to you coming by, sir!
Sir! Come and visit the market again too,
please!
Step right up, step right up!
Emil's got better goods at lower prices
than any other shop, for every customer!
Well, well, what a fine gentleman.
How about a piece of fruit?
Cheap, fresh, and the taste can't be beat!
I'll take one.
Why take just one? Take a whole bag home
with you. Don't worry, same price is fine.
In return, come back and see me again!
note: Msg 79820: #2042 follows on a new line (needs variant 'Young master!' there); msg 79343 uses #2042 after NAME as ', young master!'.

en: Well now, sir, we've met before, haven't we?
When you're a merchant, you remember your
customers' faces, you know.
How about some tomatoes today?
Well, why not. I'll take one.
Why take just one? Take a whole bag home
with you. Don't worry, same price is fine.
Thanks again, sir!
Hey, sir! Welcome!!
At this market, you'll find anything you need
for daily life. Go on, take a look, sir!
(This might be a good place to find someone to drink from, too...)
Don't go looking elsewhere, sir.
Not when there's such fine merchandise
note: Continues into M1#2000 (slice 025): must read 'right in front of you.' (lined up/after all omitted).
